summary: The sparse target-flag optimization preserves target assignments for records whose status is observed, and the revised diagnostic fixes the defects identified in the previous review. However, the production builder is still known to terminate on 436 fallback inconsistencies, so these changes cannot yet produce the target-only linkage run. It also treats 4.8 million records lacking an observed Ancestry–FamilySearch comparison as non-target, an assumption that needs a sensitivity check before interpreting the run as a clean target-only counterfactual.

findings.title: The target-only builder still exits on 436 known fallback inconsistencies
findings.what_the_code_does: The builder counts records satisfying `name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans)` into `nbad`, then executes `exit 459` whenever `nbad>0`. The review brief records that the current inputs produce `nbad==436`; the new diagnostic describes those records but does not change the builder or resolve their inconsistent fallback names.
findings.why_it_matters: On the documented current inputs, the script stops after processing the divided files and cannot complete the target-only linkage pipeline. More substantively, selecting either version of these 436 names without understanding the discrepancy could change candidate matches, so simply removing the assertion would not be safe.
findings.how_to_check: Run `replication/Run-Stata.ps1 MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do`, inspect the 436 listed records, and then rerun `replication/Run-Stata.ps1 MATCHING/_tgt_only_run.do`; confirm that `CHECK: 436 ... differ` is followed by return code 459.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the diagnostic to determine why the two cleaning paths differ. Harmonize the relevant cleaning step or explicitly select and document the intended Ancestry fallback, then retain the assertion and verify that `nbad==0` before rerunning the linkage pipeline.

findings.title: Millions of records without measured target status are assigned to the non-target group
findings.what_the_code_does: Target status is observed only in `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` through `tgt = !(namefrst==namefrst_fs & namelast==namelast_fs)`. The saved flag contains only observed targets, and every divided-file record unmatched to it receives `tgt=0`; this combines known Ancestry–FamilySearch agreements with the 4,819,575 records reported in the brief as absent from the labeled dataset.
findings.why_it_matters: For those 4.8 million records, the code has not established that the two commercial sources agree. Giving all of them Ancestry names may affect both their own links and other records' links through candidate competition. Consequently, the resulting comparison is target-only replacement within the labeled universe, not necessarily replacement only where the paper's disagreement criterion is false across the full linkage universe.
findings.how_to_check: Merge all divided-file IDs to the complete labeled-data ID list and tabulate the three groups: observed target, observed non-target, and target status unavailable. Rerun linkage under at least two treatments of the unavailable group—Ancestry fallback and model names—and compare link counts, precision/recall, and changed matches.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve an explicit third status for records absent from the labeled data. Either obtain the commercial-name comparison needed to classify them, restrict and clearly label the estimand, or report sensitivity results showing that how this group is handled does not drive the target-only comparison.

verified_clean.item: The sparse target flag preserves assignments for records with observed target status.
verified_clean.evidence: Observed targets are retained before saving, merge matches retain `tgt==1`, and all unmatched master observations are assigned zero at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:54-65 and MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:100-103.

verified_clean.item: The production sources are checked for identical file sets, unique IDs, and identical record membership.
verified_clean.evidence: Filename lists are sorted and compared at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:71-81; both inputs receive `isid id`, and their merge requires `assert(3)` at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:91-103.

verified_clean.item: The revised diagnostic now uses the complete labeled-data ID universe rather than the sparse target flag.
verified_clean.evidence: It loads every `histid` directly from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` before testing `_merge==1` at MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:17-22 and MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:44-46.

verified_clean.item: Both diagnostic accumulators use their correct counters and handle empty results.
verified_clean.evidence: The discrepancy and nonmembership batches use `zb` and `zn` respectively at MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:36-51, while output blocks are guarded by those counters at MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:57-86.

verified_clean.item: The diagnostic handles Stata's numeric missing-value ordering correctly in its age categories.
verified_clean.evidence: The categories are `age<10`, `age>=10 & age<.`, and `age>=.` at MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:89-94.

verified_clean.item: The change introduces no estimator, standard-error calculation, treatment assignment, or causal-effect calculation requiring an additional inference review.
verified_clean.evidence: The executable changes construct name inputs and descriptive diagnostics; substitution occurs at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:111-124.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so paper claims could not be checked against the code; claims-vs-code review was limited to claims in comments and the review brief.
The external census and divided-file datasets were unavailable, so the reported counts and resulting linkage changes could not be independently recalculated.
The Stata pipeline could not be executed; runtime conclusions rely on source logic and the run outcome documented in review/briefs/2026-11-17-tgt-diag.md.
This was a diff-scoped review of the uncommitted working tree, including the untracked files reported by `git status --short`, not a full-repository audit.
